subject: Custody preference check-in: Dedicated vs Private VPC for MedLytics
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@medlytics.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@medlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Custody preference check-in: Dedicated vs Private VPC for MedLytics

Hi Lena / Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what I heard and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem):

Key constraints you mentioned:
- MedLytics will process patient-level data (PHI) for model inference in the POC.
- You need cryptographic separation of customer keys (HSM/KMS integration).
- Audit logs and access trails must be kept for 1 year but purged from any analytics store within 30 days.
- Residency requirement: US-East for primary processing.

My read: Private VPC (customer-managed VPC or on-prem package) is the likeliest candidate given the KMS/HSM and PHI notes, but Dedicated reserved capacity with strict custody controls could work if we can guarantee isolated compute and customer-managed keying. To make a recommendation we need to confirm a couple items:

1) Data in-scope: Will raw PHI ever be persisted outside of RAM/KV cache (e.g., logs, payload storage, embeddings)?
2) Key ownership: Do you require Redwood to use customer-managed KMS/HSM for model encryption and disk encryption, or is a Redwood-managed KMS acceptable with an audit trail?
3) Network: Do you require a private peering/VPC endpoint (no public internet egress) and a static egress IP range?
4) Compliance artifacts: Do you have a SOC 2 / security questionnaire we should return? We can attach our SOC 2 report under NDA.

Proposed next step: 45-minute security + infra workshop (Redwood security, our infra lead Marissa, and your security/infra) to align on gaps and a mutual action plan. I attached a short deployment checklist and our SOC2 question stub to speed review. Please confirm which of these slots works for you:
- Tue Jul 13, 10:00–10:45 PT
- Wed Jul 14, 14:00–14:45 PT
- Thu Jul 15, 09:30–10:15 PT

If you already lean Private VPC, say so and we’ll prepare a private deployment runbook and rough cost delta versus Dedicated for the POC.

Attachments: redwood-deployment-checklist.xlsx (XLSX), medlytics-soc2-questions.pdf (PDF)

Thanks —

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0192
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@medlytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@medlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 13:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Custody preference check-in: Dedicated vs Private VPC for MedLytics

Tessa —

Appreciate the recap. Quick answers:

1) Data in-scope: yes — for the POC we'll send representative PHI payloads (de-identified where possible), but we want to assume PHI will be present and design for that. No embeddings should be retained beyond session lifetime unless explicitly agreed.
2) Key ownership: we require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) for disk and model artifact encryption. HSM-backed keys preferred.
3) Network: private peering (VPC endpoint) is required. No public internet egress for inference traffic. Static egress IPs are helpful for allow-listing.
4) Compliance: attaching our security questionnaire (separate doc). We need your SOC 2 and penetration test summary under NDA.

Other asks:
- Can you confirm retention for logs vs payload — we need PB-level logs purged from analytics within 30 days and access logs preserved for 1 year in a tamper-evident store.
- SLA: what's the baseline latency SLO for Private VPC (p95 token latency) and the SLA you support for Dedicated vs Private?
- Cost: rough uplift for Private VPC (with customer KMS and dedicated GPUs) vs Dedicated for a small-MVP (3 rtx6000-class GPUs) — a back-of-envelope estimate is fine for now.

We can do Tue Jul 13 10:00 PT. Invited Samir and I will bring our infra/security.

Best,

Lena Ortiz
Head of Integrations
MedLytics, Inc.
Phone: (212) 555-0133
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Custody preference check-in: Dedicated vs Private VPC for MedLytics

Tessa / Ben —

Thanks for the summary, Tessa. Short internal notes before we meet with MedLytics:

- Recommendation: Start the POC on Private VPC (VPC connector + customer-managed KMS) given PHI and the no-public-egress requirement. This lets us satisfy HSM/KMS key ownership and VPC isolation without immediate on-prem engineering.
- Config notes: We can configure a Private VPC deployment using our Private offering with the following: pinned model version, dedicated GPU pool (3 units), mandatory KMS integration (customer-supplied), and a retention policy that purges analytics/derived embeddings after 30 days while keeping access logs in the audit store for 12 months.
- SLA/Cost: For a dedicated 3-GPU Private VPC POC, expect an uplift of approximately 30–45% versus standard Dedicated per-token costs, plus a modest setup fee (encryption integration + network peering). We should present a low/high estimate. SLA target: 99.9% availability; p95 token latencies depend on model size — we should propose a performance profile once we pick the model.

Ben — can you draft a one-page mutual action plan (timeline, responsibilities, gating items: KMS proofs, security workshop, NDA/soc2 transfer) and a ballpark cost range by EOD Mon? I can take the tech runbook and fill deployment steps.

Marissa
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Requests for you prior to the call:

- Share your security questionnaire or a placeholder if you haven't yet (Doc attached if handy).
